title: Mexico and Central America
objective: After this level you can describe the volcanoes, highlands and coasts of Mexico and Central America.
summary: Plates meet under Mexico and Central America, so volcanoes are everywhere. Mexico's heartland is a high plateau, and Central America is a narrow isthmus with a wet Caribbean coast.

cards.headline: In 1943, a volcano was born in a farmer's cornfield.
cards.body: On February 20, the ground in Dionisio Pulido's field in Mexico cracked open and started throwing out ash. The new volcano, Parícutin, kept erupting for 9 years. Definitely not the crop he planted.

cards.headline: Volcano country
cards.body: Mexico is volcano country. An active volcanic belt crosses central Mexico, and its peaks include Citlaltépetl (also called Orizaba), a volcano that is Mexico's highest point. Farther south, some 40 volcanic cones line Central America's Pacific side. The cause is underground: several of Earth's plates meet here and press on each other, so the ground shakes and volcanoes grow.

cards.headline: Life on the high table
cards.body: Between two long ranges, the Sierra Madre Occidental in the west and the Sierra Madre Oriental in the east, lies the Mexican Plateau. It's Mexico's largest and most densely populated region. Near its southern end, around Mexico City, the land rises about 2,100 to 2,700 m above sea level. Mexico's heartland isn't a coastal plain; it's a high tabletop between mountains.

cards.headline: A bridge between continents
cards.body: South of Mexico, the land narrows into Central America, an isthmus that links North and South America. At its narrowest, in Panama, it's only about 50 km wide. Its two coasts don't get the same weather, either: the Caribbean side receives about twice as much rain as the Pacific side. Two oceans, one short drive apart.

mascot.line: Keep the word isthmus: here, the narrow land bridge linking North and South America.

questions.prompt: Which region, between the two Sierra Madre ranges, is Mexico's largest and most densely populated?

options.label: The Pacific coast
options.rationale: The coast lies outside the two ranges.

options.label: The Caribbean coast
options.rationale: The heartland is high ground, not coast.

questions.explanation: The Mexican Plateau sits between the Sierra Madre Occidental and Oriental, and it's Mexico's largest and most densely populated region.

questions.prompt: Why do Mexico and Central America have so many volcanoes and earthquakes?

options.label: Several plates meet and press together
They sit inside the warm tropics
The Caribbean coast gets heavy rain

questions.explanation: Several plates meet under the region and press on each other, which brings frequent earthquakes and eruptions.

questions.prompt: From Level 15: the volcanoes lining Central America's Pacific side belong to which great chain?

options.label: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge
options.rationale: That seam runs down the Atlantic, not the Pacific rim.

options.label: The Great Rift Valley
options.rationale: That's in East Africa, far from the Pacific.

questions.explanation: Central America's Pacific-side volcanoes sit where plates meet on the rim of the Pacific: the Ring of Fire, home to about 75% of Earth's volcanoes.
